title: Readiness burnup, velocity, and fallback rotations
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, tactical runbook for the immediate next-6-week launch window. It combines a lightweight burnup-style tracker for readiness tasks, a small set of velocity KPIs to watch during ramp, and a rotating owner matrix for fallback/operational handoffs. Goal: give on-call/product-ops an actionable single-pane that is easy to scan during daily standups and launch war-room moments.

Context + what this is NOT:
- NOT a full roadmap or product PRD. This is an operational cadence artifact focused on go/no-go signals and quick escalation paths.
- Mirrors signals from the main launch playbook but prioritizes the top 12 items that block a minimum viable production launch.

Quick signals (top-of-mind metrics to surface every standup):
- Blocking tickets (severity >= P1) count and owner
- End-to-end pipeline: % of acceptance tests passing on staging (target >= 95%)
- Mean 95th latency for representative user flow (target < 300ms gen step)
- Cost burn per 100k tokens vs baseline (alert if > +25%)
- Canary error rate vs baseline (alert if > 3x)

Mini burnup tracker (weekly snapshots) — interpret as: completed items / total scope for launch-MVP. Update once per weekday standup.
- Week start (2024-10-14): 6/24
- Week 2 (2024-10-21): 9/24
- Week 3 (2024-10-28): 13/24
- Week 4 (2024-11-04): 17/24
- Week 5 (2024-11-11): 21/24
- Week 6 target (2024-11-18): 24/24 (green = ready)

High-impact items in tracker (explicit owners & blocking criteria):
1) Canary routing policy + automatic fallback — owner: Marco Ruiz — blocking if canary traffic cannot be rerouted within 5m without state loss.
2) KV cache persistence validation on dedicated nodes — owner: Elena Gomez — blocking if KV restore tests fail on cold-start.
3) Cost telemetry hooks for token-level attribution — owner: Aisha Patel — blocking if token attribution is missing for > 30% of routes.
4) RBAC + KMS integration smoke tests for Private deployments — owner: Samir Khanna — blocking if key rotation simulation fails.
5) Console rollout dashboard: per-route latency and token spend widgets — owner: Pedro Li — blocking if dashboard data delay >10m.
(others tracked in the board; update owners if reassigned)

Velocity KPIs to monitor (live):
- Ticket throughput: closed P2+ per day (target >= 6 during ramp week)
- Regression alerts per 1000 evals (target <= 0.5)
- Median lead time for bug -> fix -> deploy (target < 1 day during launch week)
- Canary progression velocity: % of target traffic per hour (target: double traffic every 4 hours if no alerts)

Fallback rotations (owner schedule) — 7-day cadence, primary + backup, rotate Fridays at 17:00 PT
- Rotation A (2024-11-01 to 2024-11-07): primary Marco Ruiz, backup Elena Gomez
- Rotation B (2024-11-08 to 2024-11-14): primary Aisha Patel, backup Samir Khanna
- Instructions for rotation change: update Slack #launch-ops topic, update on-call calendar, ping SRE handoff thread.

Preflight Go/No-Go checklist (must be green or have documented mitigations):
- Stability: < 1 P1 in last 72h and noise floor under threshold
- Performance: 95th latency within SLO on staging and dedicated (binary pass/fail set for key flows)
- Cost: projected per-token cost delta within 15% of commitment model OR explicit funding signed off by finance
- Observability: traces, logs, alerting and sampling policy validated end-to-end
- Security: KMS rotation test passed, audit logs enabled, baseline pen-test items triaged
- Rollback: tested rollback path that restores pinned model/version within 10m
- Customer communications: support playbook + pre-drafted email + status page templates ready

Canary orchestration quick-play (recommended cadence):
1) Start at 0.5% production traffic for 1 hour (smoke). Validate errors, 95th latency, and cost signal.
2) If green, 2% for 2 hours. Validate again and run a lightweight load test.
3) 8% for 4 hours. Monitor cohort-specific quality metrics (semantic fidelity, token drift).
4) 25% for 8 hours. Run parallel traffic to Dedicated and Hosted paths to validate routing policies.
5) Full release. Maintain high-sensitivity monitoring for 48h and be ready to rollback on any single metric breach.

Escalation play (who to call first):
- Customer-visible regressions (errors = >1% for 30m): product-ops -> SRE lead -> infra on-call -> eng-owner
- Cost blowout (delta > +35% sustained for 30m): finance observer -> product-ops -> infra (throttle)
- Data leakage suspicion: security on-call immediate (do not perform triage in public channels)

Quick tactical mitigations for common launch failures:
- Spike in latency: throttle new long-seq requests by feature-flagging sequence-length cap, scale serving pool by +1 set, roll forward smaller model variant if available.
- Higher error rate on canary: cut traffic by half, switch canary traffic to fallback model variant, open P1, start postmortem timer.
- Observability lag: switch to lower sampling rate on non-essential traces, add temporary verbose logs for failing route, notify console dashboard owner to sanity-check ingestion.

Notes to self / open questions (sticky items for product-ops):
- Should we add a lightweight quality evaluation (human-in-the-loop) at 8% canary? (pro: catches semantic regressions; con: slows ramp)
- Confirm finance approval path for emergency burst capacity (who signs in evenings?)
- Add a small synthetic user cohort with long context sequences to test KV cache durability under real traffic patterns.

Immediate next actions (today):
- Marco: validate canary reroute in staging and document steps (by EOD)
- Elena: run KV cold-start restore matrix and post results to this doc (by EOD)
- Aisha: wire missing token attribution for two high-traffic routes (PR and smoke)
- Samir: run KMS rotation smoke and confirm no regression (overnight)

Appendix: Where to find the canonical artifacts
- Main launch playbook (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/launch-playbook
- Launch Jira board: JIRA-4321 (board link in Confluence)
- Infra/config PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pulls?q=is%3Apr+label%3Alaunch

If anything here is unclear or you want a tighter digest for pager duty, ping me in Slack @aisha (I will maintain a short daily summary).
